sources.title: Supporting small business relief
sources.verified_claim: The current scheme limits eligible 2026-27 bill increases after revaluation using £800 or percentage caps depending on rateable value. Eligibility depends on the actual business property and prior relief position, neither of which is established for a sample parcel.

sources.title: Transitional relief
sources.verified_claim: Government transitional relief phases in qualifying bill increases from the 1 April 2026 revaluation using rateable-value bands. The rule cannot produce a parcel liability without an actual hereditament and valuation.

sources.title: Business Rates Relief: 2026 Supporting Small Business Relief, local authority guidance
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: The updated guidance sets eligibility and reimbursement rules for billing authorities administering 2026 SSBR through 2028-29. Administrative guidance does not establish candidate-property eligibility.

sources.title: National non-domestic rates collected by councils in England: forecast for 2026 to 2027
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: The national forecast describes expected non-domestic-rate collections and changes in reliefs for 2026-27. National fiscal totals are not a borough tax-base estimate or parcel liability.

sources.title: Business rates revaluation 2026
sources.publisher: Valuation Office Agency / HM Revenue & Customs
sources.verified_claim: VOA confirms new rateable values took effect from 1 April 2026 and explains that rateable value is not the same as rent or the final rates bill. No sample-parcel rateable value is inferred without an exact property match.

sources.title: Business rates revaluation 2026
sources.verified_claim: Enfield publishes the five 2026-27 multipliers, transitional surcharge and relief changes. Borough billing information does not establish a business hereditament or liability at parcel_30762.

sources.title: Business Rates
sources.verified_claim: Havering explains the 1 April 2026 revaluation, multiplier changes, Supporting Small Business scheme and other reliefs. Actual liability at parcel_46142 depends on occupation, valuation and use not yet bound to the parcel.

sources.title: Business rates 2026 revaluation
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth explains that 2026 rateable values use the 1 April 2024 valuation date and that a rateable-value increase does not necessarily translate proportionally into a bill increase. No value or liability is inferred for parcel_61522.
